subject: plan §1.9 L-12 / D-28 — writer timeout claim; and the §15 'timeout source' field
claim: L-12: 'default writer timeout 600 s against measured 30 h heavy builds unless writer_timeout_seconds is set per asset (runner.py:89; set on ~2 of 128)'

angles.method: live production count of writer_timeout_seconds
angles.result: REFUTED — 128 of 128 assets carry a non-null writer_timeout_seconds; 107 of 128 carry a NON-DEFAULT value (column default is 600). Distribution: 10800s x91, 600s x21, 60s x5, 120s x5, 1800s x2, 300s x1, 3600s x1, 21600s x1 (ka_gochara_sweep), 86400s x1 (ka_kshetra). The claim '~2 of 128' is wrong by a factor of ~50.

angles.method: column definition check
angles.result: information_schema: asset_registry.writer_timeout_seconds integer DEFAULT 600. So 'set' must mean non-default; on that reading it is 107/128, not 2/128. The 21 assets at 600 are the ones sitting on the bare default.

angles.method: registered timeout vs the asset's OWN measured worst-case run (clean telemetry only; D-13-POLLUTED rows excluded)
angles.result: A SHARPER REAL DEFECT — 7 assets have a registered timeout BELOW their own measured worst run: ka_gochara 0.50h vs 6.50h (13.0x), bo_laksana 3.00h vs 19.20h (6.4x), ka_gochara_sweep 6.00h vs 35.60h (5.9x), ga_strength 3.00h vs 13.10h (4.4x), ga_sensitive 3.00h vs 6.40h (2.1x), bo_laksana_rerank 0.17h vs 0.35h (2.1x), ka_kshetra 24.00h vs 33.80h (1.4x). Five are tier H (heavy partitioned) or X (generation-bearing).

angles.method: registered timeout vs p90
angles.result: bo_laksana_rerank: timeout 600s (bare default) vs p90 20m — the watchdog is expected to kill it on more than 1 run in 10, not merely in the tail.

angles.method: the generated §15 'timeout source' field
angles.result: FAIL — the field reads 'registered' for all 128 assets, including the 21 sitting at the bare column default. §15 defines the vocabulary as registered | telemetry-derived | default. Because the generator tests only non-null and the column defaults to 600, the field can NEVER emit 'default' or 'telemetry-derived'. It is a constant wearing the clothes of a measurement — an §N.8/H4 earned-signal violation inside the campaign's own control surface.

evidence: SELECT count(*) FROM asset_registry WHERE writer_timeout_seconds IS NOT NULL -> 128
SELECT writer_timeout_seconds, count(*) FROM asset_registry GROUP BY 1 -> 10800:91, 600:21, 60:5, 120:5, 1800:2, 300:1, 3600:1, 21600:1, 86400:1
join of live asset_registry.writer_timeout_seconds against workbook Asset Register Worst/P90/Telemetry, POLLUTED excluded -> 7 assets under worst, 1 under p90
regex count of '**timeout source:**' values inside plan ASSET_PLANS markers -> Counter({'registered': 128})
correct_statement_of_the_defect: Not 'timeouts are unset'. Timeouts ARE set, deliberately, on 107 of 128 — and 7 of them, concentrated in exactly the heavy and generation-bearing tiers, are set BELOW the asset's own measured worst-case runtime. A set-but-too-low ceiling is worse than an unset one because it reads as honest configuration while reliably killing the longest builds; it is a plausible direct contributor to the 45.6% completion rate L-12 attributes to the opposite cause.
impact: Two consequences. (1) §8.6 stage 2 derives timeouts per rung: R1 (ga_strength, ga_sensitive), R2 (bo_laksana, bo_laksana_rerank) and R3 (ka_gochara, ka_gochara_sweep, ka_kshetra) each open with a named, quantified timeout defect rather than a generic 'derive timeouts' task. (2) L-12/D-28's stated evidence is false and should be restated; the defect survives in stronger form, so this is a correction, not a retraction.

subject: M0-T11 — migrate.ts entrypoint guard (F-2), commit 1089db9b6
claim: migrate.ts's main() runs only when the module is the process entrypoint, never as an import side effect; both directions covered by a real detector
verdict_qualifier: PASS on the claim as stated. One named residual (RES-1) is NOT a defect in T11 and does not block it, but the builder's characterisation of that residual as a 'loud' failure is refuted below and must not stand.

angles.method: 1. code read — is main() the only top-level side effect?
angles.result: PASS — scripts/migrate.ts:766 `if (isDirectEntrypoint(import.meta.url, process.argv[1])) { main() }` is the sole top-level statement. The only other lines matching a top-level-statement grep (42, 64) are inside the TRACKER_DDL template literal, not statements. So guarding main() guards the whole import surface; there is no second side effect left unguarded.

angles.method: 2. independent re-run of the suite (not reading the builder's transcript)
angles.result: PASS — `npx vitest run scripts/__tests__/migrate_entrypoint_guard.test.ts`: 2 files/2 tests passed, 370ms.

angles.method: 3. MY OWN bidirectional mutation proof (I16 — did not reuse the builder's)
angles.result: PASS — baseline sha256 abe90a7d03242e82967a5d633f73c5e1c09404395e80c11d8a30aca619fd60ff. Mutation A `if (true || isDirectEntrypoint(...))` (re-introduces the F-2 hazard) -> test A FAILS. Mutation B `if (false && isDirectEntrypoint(...))` (silent no-op) -> test B FAILS. Restored from byte-copy; sha256 identical and `git diff --quiet scripts/migrate.ts` exit 0. The detector fails in BOTH directions, so it is real, not a test that passes either way.

angles.method: 4. does CI actually run this test? (a guard CI never runs is a §N.8 non-detector)
angles.result: PASS — ci.yml:172 `npm test` = package.json `vitest run`, no path filter. vitest.config.ts's `node` project declares no `include`, so vitest's default glob applies and matches scripts/__tests__/; the path is absent from SHARED_EXCLUDE and from DOM_TEST_GLOBS. `tsx` is a devDependency (^4.0.0) so node_modules/.bin/tsx exists after npm ci. A missing binary would fail loudly, not vacuously: both tests assert positive content (toContain('IMPORTED_OK function'); toMatch(/ECONNREFUSED/)), so an ENOENT empty result fails them.

angles.method: 5. `--target` — conductor's Q2, unexercised by the builder, a binding D-9 condition on applying 590
angles.result: PASS — exercised against an explicitly unreachable DB (127.0.0.1:1, env built with `env -i`). `--target 590` enters main() (ECONNREFUSED at pool.connect). So do `--dry-run` and the bare form, from three cwd spellings (platform/, repo root, /tmp with an absolute path). 5/5 entered main().

angles.method: 6. symlinks — conductor's Q5, reasoned by the builder but never constructed
angles.result: PASS, now experimental — run through a symlinked directory (relative and absolute spellings) and as a symlinked FILE: all 3 enter main(). The /tmp -> /private/tmp realpath case also enters main(), with the stack reading `at async main (/private/tmp/.../scripts/migrate.ts:702)` — proving the realpathSync normalisation is load-bearing and correct. NOTE: my first attempt at this case reported a NO-OP; that was my own probe copying the scripts tree without node_modules so `pg` could not resolve. Re-run with deps resolvable, it entered main(). Corrected before reporting, not after.

angles.method: 7. cross-version — conductor's Q4, 'CI-runner behaviour is inferred'
angles.result: PASS, materially strengthened — re-ran both directions on Node v18.20.8 as well as v24.14.0. The runner's Node 20 lies BETWEEN the two verified majors. Direct run on Node 18: main() entered. Import on Node 18: printed `IMPORTED_OK function` AND no ECONNREFUSED — a POSITIVE observation (the module evaluated to completion) paired with the absence, not a bare absence.

angles.method: 8. conductor's Q1 — is absence-of-connect-attempt sufficient evidence?
angles.result: SUFFICIENT, and here is why it is not a vacuum: (a) angle 3 shows test A DOES fail when the migrator runs, so the absence is produced by a working detector; (b) test A pairs the absence with a positive assertion that the import resolved and returned a usable function, so the module provably evaluated to completion — had the guard been true, main() would have run. The builder's refusal to point a run at a real database was correct and I did not relax it either: every run I made used 127.0.0.1:1 supplied explicitly through `env -i`. Live demonstration of the hazard the conductor was right to flag: my own first Node-18 probe printed 'import did NOT run the migrator' purely because `timeout` was missing from my stripped PATH and nothing executed at all. An absence assertion without a paired positive is worthless; test A has the pairing.

angles.method: 9. conductor's Q3 — tsconfig coverage
angles.result: CONFIRMED as the builder stated — platform/tsconfig.json `exclude: ['node_modules','scripts']`. The project-wide typecheck genuinely never covered this file, before or after T11. A pre-existing CI coverage gap, not a T11 defect; recorded so nobody later mistakes `tsc -p tsconfig.json` passing for evidence about this file.

angles.method: 10. ADVERSARIAL — is the false-negative failure mode really 'loud'? (the builder's §6.1 claim, and the code comment's own words)
angles.result: REFUTED. deploy.yml:326-335 runs `cd platform && npx tsx scripts/migrate.ts` with NO post-run assertion. main()'s success path prints NOTHING when nothing is pending: `ran` is empty, so `ran.forEach(name => console.log('Applied: '+name))` emits zero lines and the process exits 0 (migrate.ts:704-710). Therefore 'migrations already up to date' and 'the migrator never ran' produce BYTE-IDENTICAL CI output — nothing, exit 0 — and deploy-web then proceeds on `needs: [migrate]`. That is CLAUDE.md §N.4's named hazard verbatim: migrations silently doing nothing while the deploy reports success. The in-code comment at migrate.ts:730 even contradicts itself, calling the same outcome 'exit silently and loudly wrong'.

evidence: shasum -a 256 scripts/migrate.ts before/after mutation cycle -> abe90a7d03242e82967a5d633f73c5e1c09404395e80c11d8a30aca619fd60ff both times; git diff --quiet exit 0
mutation `if (true || ...)` -> test A fails; mutation `if (false && ...)` -> test B fails (both run by PARIKSAKA, not quoted from the builder)
ci.yml:172 `npm test`; platform/package.json scripts.test = 'vitest run'; vitest.config.ts node project has no include key
8 subprocess invocations (3 cwd spellings x {bare,--dry-run,--target 590}, 3 symlink forms, 1 /private/tmp realpath) all -> ECONNREFUSED at pool.connect = main() entered
Node v18.20.8 direct run -> main() entered; Node v18.20.8 import -> 'IMPORTED_OK function', no ECONNREFUSED
deploy.yml:326-335 — no assertion after `npx tsx scripts/migrate.ts`

residual.statement: A wrongly-false isDirectEntrypoint on the CI runner would make the production migrate step a silent green no-op, indistinguishable in the log from a legitimate up-to-date run, after which deploy-web ships against an unmigrated schema. T11's direction choice is CORRECT (a false positive migrates production from an import; a false negative skips a deploy) and I am not asking for it to be reversed. But the residual has no detector, which is §N.8, and it must not be recorded as 'loud'. Cheapest honest fixes, in preference order: (a) assert in deploy.yml that the migrator ran (have main() print a terminal sentinel unconditionally and grep for it), or (b) have migrate.ts exit non-zero with a diagnostic when it is not the entrypoint AND argv[1] resolves to a file whose basename is migrate.ts. Note the risk PROFILE changed: pre-T11 the deploy path's condition (NODE_ENV !== 'test') was trivially true on the runner; post-T11 it depends on a realpath comparison never executed on that platform. Angle 7 narrows that gap to Node 20 specifically, bracketed by two verified majors.

recommendation: DISPATCH THE MIGRATION WAVE. T11's claim is certified; T12 (apply 590) and T13 (register 588/589) are safe to run — the direct-run direction is the one they exercise and it is verified across 8 invocation spellings and 2 Node majors, --target included. RES-1 concerns the deploy path only and should be a separate work item, not a hold on the wave.
